subject: gk
question: What is the fiscal year period in India?

options.text: 1st April of a year to 31st March of the next upcoming year
1st April to 31st December of the same year
1st January to 31st December of the same year
1st January of a year to 31st December of the next upcoming year

solution:
The correct answer is __**1st April of a year to 31st March of the next upcoming year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A fiscal year is a 12-month period** used by governments and businesses for financial reporting and budgeting purposes. In India, the fiscal year period is from 1st April of a year to 31st March of the next upcoming year.
 
• The Indian fiscal year is also known as the financial year. It is used to calculate income tax, goods and services tax (GST), and other taxes and duties.
 
• In government accounting—which varies by nation—and for budgetary purposes, a fiscal year—also known as a financial year or occasionally a budget year—is utilized. Financial reporting by companies and other organizations is another use for it.
 
• Many jurisdictions have laws requiring businesses to compile and publish yearly financial reports, however, typically the reporting period does not coincide with the calendar year.
 
• Accounting records must normally be kept up to date, and taxes must be computed annually in accordance with tax rules, which often align with the fiscal year utilized by the government. Annual tax calculations are particularly important for direct taxes like income tax. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The British colonial government **established the** present fiscal year in 1867** to harmonize India's fiscal year with the British Empire's.
 
• India used to have a fiscal year that extended from May 1 to April 30 before 1867.
 
• The LK Jha committee suggested establishing a fiscal year that began on January 1 and ended on December 31 in 1984.
 
• The government, however, decided against implementing this idea out of concern for potential problems during the transition time.
